newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares fall in holiday-hit end-account trade.
newsitem.headline: India shares fall in holiday-hit end-account trade.

text.p: Indian shares finished lower on Friday hit by business-squaring and little fresh support forthcoming because of the Good Friday holiday, brokers said.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 72.05 points or 1.93 percent to 3,663.53.
"Institutions are not active in the market. This fall has taken everyone by surprise," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at local firm, Lloyds Securities.
The absence of any fund activity ahead of the long Easter week-end and a holiday at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) gave bear operators the upper hand, dealers said.
The Delhi exchange was also undermined by the close of weekly account, traders said.
The Delhi index lost 11.46 points to 769.14.
"Operators were unable to manage funds to take deliveries and were forced to unload their positions," said S.C. Juneja at Delhi brokerage Jaico Credit.

Traders said the absence of foreign buying, and reluctance of speculators and investors to stake fresh claims ahead of the end of the current financial year on March 31 also pushed share prices lower.
Traders expect the market rally next week as fresh demand picks up with the beginning of new fiscal year on April 1.
"The market looks good for a rally," said Yogendra Shah, director at brokerage YSN Shares Pvt Ltd. "I expect fund demand in side-counters to rise."
Shares of shoe-maker Bata India ended 4.25 rupees, or 6.4 percent, higher at 71.0 rupees after the firm on Thursday announced profits.
Bata India unveiled a net profit of 41.5 million rupees for calendar 1996 against net loss of 421.6 million rupees in 1995.
